# Further Reading {#sec-further-reading .appendix}

This is a selective reading list for the revised book, not a systematic literature review. Research findings depend on the models, participants and tasks studied. None of these sources validates the fictional PDP-2026.1 pack or its illustrative marking threshold.

## Models, context and prompting

- OpenAI (2023), [GPT-4 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.08774). Describes the evaluated model and limitations; it does not disclose the parameter count. Distinguish the model from a current chat product.
- Liu, N. F. and colleagues (2024), [Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172). Investigates sensitivity to the position of relevant information. A large context window is not a guarantee of reliable use of every source.
- Xu, Xiaohan and colleagues (2024), [Re-Reading Improves Reasoning in Large Language Models](https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.871/), *EMNLP*, 15549–15575. Reports a rereading method on tested benchmarks, not a universal rule that two repetitions are optimal for every task.
- Vaswani, A. and colleagues (2017), [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762). The transformer architecture paper; architectural history is distinct from evidence of educational benefit.

## Learning and judgement

- Bastani, H. and colleagues (2025), [Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning](https://hamsabastani.github.io/education_llm.pdf). The high-school mathematics study distinguishes performance while supported from later unaided performance. Its setting should not be silently generalised to all business courses.
- Wineburg, S. and McGrew, S. (2019), [Lateral Reading and the Nature of Expertise: Reading Less and Learning More When Evaluating Digital Information](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/016146811912101102). Relevant to checking a claim beyond the page or generated answer presenting it.
- Dawson, P. (2017), [Assessment rubrics: towards clearer and more replicable design, research and practice](https://doi.org/10.1080/02602938.2015.1111294), *Assessment & Evaluation in Higher Education*, 42(3), 347–360. Useful for specifying rubric design decisions; it is not an endorsement of this book's sample rubric.
- TEQSA (2025), [Enacting assessment reform in a time of artificial intelligence](https://www.teqsa.gov.au/sites/default/files/2025-09/enacting-assessment-reform-in-a-time-of-artificial-intelligence.pdf). Sets out multiple approaches to assessment reform. It does not require a particular transcript metric, grade weighting or universal AI ban.

## Data handling and product boundaries

- Office of the Australian Information Commissioner, [Guidance on privacy and the use of commercially available AI products](https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/guidance-on-privacy-and-the-use-of-commercially-available-ai-products). Start here for the Australian privacy considerations, then obtain institution-specific advice and approval.
- Microsoft, [Privacy and protections](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/privacy-and-protections). Read the scope and feature-specific conditions rather than inferring permission from an enterprise label. Product terms can change.
- Carlini, N. and colleagues (2021), [Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07805). Demonstrates training-data extraction under studied conditions.
- Nasr, M. and colleagues (2023), [Scalable Extraction of Training Data from (Production) Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17035). Further extraction research. Neither paper shows that an arbitrary private upload is necessarily retrievable by another user; neither supports a blanket impossibility claim.

## Context-specific requirements

- Fair Work Ombudsman, [Bullying and harassment](https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/bullying-and-harassment). Australian workplace guidance for checking the scope of a real issue. Fictional pack policies are not statements of law.
- European Union, [General Data Protection Regulation](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng). Consult the applicable provisions and competent advice; consent is not the only possible legal basis.
- US Department of Education, [Eligible Student Guide to FERPA](https://studentprivacy.ed.gov/resources/eligible-student-guide-family-educational-rights-and-privacy-act-ferpa). Relevant rights and exceptions require context-specific interpretation.

These links were reviewed for this September 2026 revision. Reachability is separate from applicability. Before deployment, recheck current rules, product terms and the institution's own requirements.

## Companion methodology

Michael Borck, [Conversation, Not Delegation](https://michael-borck.github.io/conversation-not-delegation), develops the wider conversation and verification approach. The present book supplies its own short recap and teaching materials; reading the companion is optional.
